title: Prove published read admission in Node Vitest

intentCoverage.report:
## Dough Intent Coverage

**Caught.** For SEED-413#published-read-admission-via-vitest at `c8dfc7ba408bf4f350984ce7875a60a8f22ce5c7`, the maintained Node assertion caught a Done catalog being accepted even though its listed blob disagreed with the published revision.

The single scratch fault at `dashboard/server/doneCatalogRead.ts:157` changed the mismatch branch to return an agreed catalog with its stale text. The published fixture for the earlier-blob case contains `done/SEED-101_gap-1.json` at pin `d4` repeated 20 times. An independent call to the production parser and handler supplied the fixture's published listing and catalog at the pinned-read boundary. It verified that the catalog named blob `b3e4b5b911820d6230bda35e7582bb711dd32507` and the listing named `9fee2e258fe2d074fd6a8bac49da93902c7e5ba4`. The original handler returned the earlier-blob gap. The faulted handler returned the stale three-record catalog and omitted the gap.

```sh
caffeinate -s -i npm run test:dashboard:backend -- \
  'observation/authenticated-read-done-catalog-gaps\.spec\.ts$' --workers=1
```

The baseline passed all 10 cases. With the fault, the earlier-blob and missing-published-record cases failed at the exact `{ revision, gap: problem }` response assertion in `dashboard/backend-tests/observation/authenticated-read-done-catalog-gaps.spec.ts:172`. Both received a catalog. The restored source matched the original bytes and clean Git state at the same revision. All 10 cases passed again and the detached scratch worktree was removed. This result covers the catalog response assertion reached by the fault. The downstream body assertions in the two failed rows did not execute.

**Next proof action**  
Retain the existing mismatch-response assertion as the proof owner for the exercised path.
